title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: Historical closure week sales: median 176 vs baseline 207.6 (x0.85); 1 occurrence.

drivers.name: Price increase (+5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Past weeks with $4.56 price: 2026-09-28 (x0.94), 2026-10-05 (x0.57); noise-adjusted avg x0.75.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A store closure on Monday (1 day) reduces demand; historical data shows similar closures reduce sales by ~15%. The price increase to $4.56 (+5.1%) is above past promotions (max 30% off), but price hikes typically reduce demand. Past price spikes (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw sales drop to 139–119 vs baseline, suggesting a ~25% demand reduction. Combining these: 0.85 (closure) × 0.75 (price) = 0.64. Evidence is moderate (2 past price spikes, 1 closure), so shrink toward 1.0. Final multiplier shrunk to 0.70. Spreads widened due to uncertainty in price effect.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.5 - 290.3 | 10%-90%: 156.3 - 281.1

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
